svg.title: Orthogonal series and outer derivation classes
svg.desc: Orthogonal positive contractions with summable commutators on a dense set define bounded derivations by a strong operator sum. Coefficient differences in c zero give explicit unitary cocycles. In the even-coordinate compact-unitization example the distance from inner star derivations is max of zero and the coefficient limsup minus min of zero and the liminf.

g.text: Orthogonal coefficients give derivations and flows
A separable C*-algebra A in B(H); H may have arbitrary dimension.
summable on a dense test set.
Real r gives a star flow
r − s ∈ c₀ gives b = h(r − s) ∈ A
Exact outer distance in A = K(ℓ²) + ℂI
h(r) has diagonal 0, r(1), 0, r(2), 0, r(3), ...
dist(d(r), Inn*(A)) = max(0, limsup r(n)) − min(0, liminf r(n))
Finite sums approximate these derivations pointwise in norm, despite the positive norm distance.
Construction: OS1–OS21. Exact distance and bounds: OS25–OS26 in Lesson 137.
Inner star derivations here are i[k, ·] with k = k* in A; the distances are operator norms on maps A → A.
